page: Amazon Web Services c7i.2xlarge is a compute-optimized Seventh-Generation instance powered by custom 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8488C processors built on x86_64 architecture. Managed under the AWS Nitro Hypervisor, the instance provides 8 vCPUs backed by 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 2 threads per core. System memory consists of 16.0 GB DDR5 RAM running at 5 GHz, allocating 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration capabilities include Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Network baseline performance is rated at 3 Gbps, while local NVMe storage is omitted entirely.

In synthetic performance evaluations, the c7i.2xlarge demonstrates solid compute and string-handling capabilities. Single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench text processing perform in the top 25% of benchmarked instances. CPU-focused workloads, such as multithreaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench software compilation with Clang, and PassMark CPU tests, register average performance. However, memory subsystem performance shows mixed results: while small-block 16 KB cached memory read bandwidth reaches 670.73 GB/sec, the overall PassMark memory score falls into the bottom 25%. Additionally, text generation for medium 7B parameter language models lands in the bottom 10% due to memory capacity and throughput constraints on larger tensor operations.

The c7i.2xlarge offers a balanced resource density for compute-heavy applications that do not require high memory-per-vCPU ratios or direct-attached ephemeral storage. Its support for AMX and AVX-512 instructions makes it efficient for low-latency batch processing, data compression, software builds, and lightweight web serving. Given its compute-focused memory ratio of 2 GB per core, it delivers cost-effective processing for distributed compute tasks and microservices, provided stateful data relies on network-attached storage.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8488C processor under the Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz, it delivers a dedicated 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include Intel AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets, a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps, and no local ephemeral storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight strong performance in single-threaded gzip compression and text processing, alongside average multi-core CPU and software compilation scores. Subsystem evaluations reveal lower comparative memory performance in PassMark testing and restricted text generation throughput for 7B parameter language models. The instance provides strong cost efficiency for CPU-bound tasks, CI/CD compilation pipelines, batch processing, static web serving, and microservices requiring dedicated compute without extensive memory overhead.
